prompt: What separates an offline test from an online one?

choices.text: Whether it is written with pytest or with a separate testing framework of its own
How long it takes to write
Whether it needs the network
Whether it is run by a person or by a pipeline

prompt: Why does it matter on which side of the apply a check sits?
hint: What has the network seen when it fails?

choices.text: Checks after the apply are more accurate
choices.why: They see other things, not more accurately.

choices.text: Checks before the apply need the router
A failure before costs nothing; a failure after is already in the network
It does not; only the order of the tests in the file matters

prompt: Put the five steps of a change in order.
What does `extra="forbid"` in the model catch?

choices.text: A key the model does not name, such as a misspelling
A value of the wrong type
A file that is not YAML
A duplicate address

prompt: How many errors did `validate.py` report for `new/edge3.yaml`?
One misspelt key, `adress`, produced two of those errors. Why two?
hint: What is missing and what is extra?

choices.text: pydantic reports every error twice
Both interfaces had the same typo, one under each of the two interface entries
`address` is missing and `adress` is not allowed
The address was also out of range, which pydantic reports against the same key

prompt: `yamllint` printed nothing; its exit status, ___, is what a pipeline reads as a pass.
Without the model, what would `ospf: p2p` have produced at render time?

choices.text: A `KeyError`
A configuration FRR refuses
An exception from StrictUndefined
An interface with no OSPF line and no error

prompt: Which functions does pytest run as tests?

choices.text: Every function in the directory
Functions named `test_*` in files named `test_*.py`
Functions decorated with `parametrize`, which is what marks a function as a test
choices.why: That multiplies a test; the name makes one.

choices.text: Functions listed by name in `pytest.ini`, next to the options for the run

prompt: Why can `test_no_address_is_used_twice` find a mistake the model cannot?

choices.text: It runs on the network
It renders the configurations first, so that it can read the addresses from FRR's own syntax
It reads every router's data at once
The model ignores addresses

prompt: How many tests did pytest collect from the three functions in `test_configs.py`?
Why was `render.py`'s loop moved under `if __name__ == "__main__":`?

choices.text: pytest refuses to import a module that has a loop at its top level
To make rendering faster, since the loop then runs only once per test session
So that importing the template does not render every file
Jinja2 requires it

prompt: Where does `test_network.py` get the number of neighbours each router should have?
hint: It is not written in the test.

choices.text: From a constant at the top of the test file, one per router
From the routers themselves, read before the change
choices.why: That would be a snapshot, which this test does not take.

choices.text: From the data: one per point-to-point interface
From NetBox, through the same token as lesson 12's scripts

prompt: Run before a change, what is the online test called, and what does it establish?
hint: A failure afterwards should be the change's.

choices.text: A unit test of the template, run before anything else in the pipeline
A dry run
A rollback
A pre-check: the network was healthy before

prompt: What can an online test find that no offline test can?

choices.text: An unplugged cable
An address used twice in the data
A routing process that did not start
A misspelt key in the data

prompt: Why did the offline tests pass the bad change?

choices.text: They were not run
Nothing in edge2's data was malformed on its own
pytest skips YAML
`passive` is not in the model, so the model let the value through without checking it
choices.why: It is one of the two allowed words.

prompt: After the bad change, edge2's own neighbour test passed. Why?
hint: Where does the test get its expectation?

choices.text: edge2 still had its neighbour, kept by OSPF until the dead interval ran out
The test only checks core1
The wrong data said edge2 should have no neighbours
SSH to edge2 failed, and pytest counts a test that cannot connect as a pass

prompt: How many seconds does OSPF wait, by default, before it declares a silent neighbour dead?
hint: The capture waited a little longer.

prompt: Twelve seconds after the revert, three tests still failed. What was the network doing?

choices.text: Converging: the routes were not installed yet
Rejecting the revert
Still running the bad configuration on edge2, since NAPALM commits after a delay
Failing a different way

prompt: What does `test_both_ends_of_a_link_agree` check that no other test did?
hint: The error was in the pair.

choices.text: That each address in the data is a valid IPv4 address with a prefix
That OSPF neighbours are `Full` on both routers at each end of every link
That both ends of each /30 run OSPF the same way
That no router has more than two interfaces in its data

prompt: An online test fails. What is the question the lesson says to ask next?

choices.text: Can the test be disabled until the network is stable again?
Who pushed last?
Is pytest up to date with the version the pipeline uses?
Could a file have shown it?

prompt: A colleague proposes running only the online tests, after each push, since they test the real network. What is lost?

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: The offline tests stop changes for free.

choices.text: Every mistake a file shows is found only after it is in the network
The ability to test more than one router
The pre-check
choices.why: Online tests can still run before the push.

prompt: Match each file to the step of a change it belongs to.
How many tests failed in the post-check run forty-five seconds after the bad change?
`pytest ___ test_configs.py` prints one line per test, each named with its parameter.
